newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: POLARTECHNICS SPIKES AS MARKET DIGESTS DEAL.
newsitem.headline: POLARTECHNICS SPIKES AS MARKET DIGESTS DEAL.

text.p: Shares in medical instrument designer Polartechnics Ltd surged 55 cents to a record high of A$4.15 on Friday as investors placed their faith in attractive valuations of the stock following the June announcement of its alliance with Ethicon Inc.
Ethicon is a unit of Johnson & Johnson and the alliance is for the commercialisation of Polartechnics' cancer detection device, the Polarprobe.
While the announcement was made in June, Polartechnics executive chairman Tony Grey told Reuters the market was only now beginning to appreciate the value of the link up.
"A few weeks ago we announced a stategic alliance with Johnson & Johnson and the market didn't react to it all that much because they didn't quite understand the import of the alliance," Grey said.
The deal sees Ethicon pay Polartechnics a total of up to US$18 million as part of the agreement, to be triggered by completion of certain milestones which it did not specify.

Polartechnics remains responsible for the manufacture and R&D operations of the Polarprobe device, with the two companies to work together to obtain regulatory approvals ahead of marketing, including in the United States and Europe.

"It is a very good deal for us. It validates the technology and our patent protection and gives us marketing credibility and ensures our financial viability," he said, adding that recent broker reports had shown a deeper understanding of the alliance, with a consequent boost in valuations.
"Finally the penny has dropped - they now realise the importance of the deal," Grey said.
By 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), Polartechnics shares were 60 cents higher at a new peak of A$4.20 on turnover of 258,176 shares.
